item.title: MS. VERSATILITY: Lake Creek's Burns can shoot, defend, lead
item.description: The versatility of Lake Creek’s Bayley Burns jumps off the game film.The junior can shoot the lights out from deep, lock down an opponent’s best player, and battle on the boards — a complete two-way threat who impacts every possession.Averaging nearly 17 points per game, Burns is one of the major keys to the Lions’ success this season.Meet Bayley Burns.

item.title: BUILDING BLOCKS: Seven Lakes' State aspirations lean heavily on Santos' evolving ingenuity
item.description: Basketball, for some, is about talent alone. For others, it's process -- a careful assembly of skills, habits, and leadership over time.At Seven Lakes, that process has been on full display in the 6-foot-5 junior, Isaiah Santos, a guard who has spent the past few seasons constructing a versatile skillset while helping elevate his team’s consistent presence. Last winter, Santos averaged just under 21 points and 10 rebounds per game en route to securing District 19-6A Offensive Player of the Year

item.title: THE POWER RANKINGS: Bowie holds off Vandegrift, Westwood in Austin area boys rankings
item.description: Bowie swept their two final non-district tuneup games to remain atop this week’s Power Rankings. Vandegrift – the only team to hang a loss on the Bulldogs -- held on for a gritty road win against #10 Vista Ridge to remain at #2 while Westwood dominated two 25-6A opponents to step over Westlake. East View, the highest-ranked 5A team, got an international win over Australia’s St. Kevin’s and a less exotic win over Copperas Cove to round out the Top 5.There was minimal movement outside the Top 5. item.description: Westlake continued to tune up for district play with a couple of nice non-district wins to remain undefeated atop our Power Rankings.
